after.problem:

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 12 \\ \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
after.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨3,0,4⟩$ and $w=⟨1,-1,1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =4i+j-3k \\  & =⟨4,1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨4,1,-3⟩.$

r=⟨3,\sqrt{7},-2⟩+t⟨-2,8,0⟩+s⟨3,-1,-1⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).

after.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-2,8,0⟩$ and $w=⟨3,-1,-1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & 8 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-8i-2j-22k \\  & =⟨-8,-2,-22⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-8,-2,-22⟩.$

content.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=⟨3,\sqrt{7},-2⟩+t⟨-2,8,0⟩+s⟨3,-1,-1⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
content.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-2,8,0⟩$ and $w=⟨3,-1,-1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & 8 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-8i-2j-22k \\  & =⟨-8,-2,-22⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-8,-2,-22⟩.$

decision.explanation: Use E=(4,-2,5) as the base point and the lines' direction vectors (7,-3,4) and (3,-5,1) as spanning vectors. They are linearly independent, so this defines a plane through E parallel to both lines.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $E(4,-2,5)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨11,0,5⟩+s⟨7,-3,4⟩$ and $r=⟨12,-2,4⟩+t⟨3,-5,1⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨7,-3,4⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨3,-5,1⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $E(4,-2,5)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $e=⟨4,-2,5⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =e+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨4,-2,5⟩+s⟨7,-3,4⟩+t⟨3,-5,1⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $U(7,-2,3),\,V(4,4,-4),$ and $W(3,7,6).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). Let's use the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{UV}$ and $\overset{\to }{UW},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{UV} & =⟨4,4,-4⟩-⟨7,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,6,-7⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{UW} & =⟨3,7,6⟩-⟨7,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,9,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $u=⟨7,-2,3⟩$ of the point $U,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =u+s\overset{\to }{UV}+t\overset{\to }{UW} \\ r & =⟨7,-2,3⟩+s⟨-3,6,-7⟩+t⟨-4,9,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). Let's use the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{UV}$ and $\overset{\to }{UW},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{UV} & =⟨4,4,-4⟩-⟨7,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,6,-7⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{UW} & =⟨3,7,6⟩-⟨7,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,9,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $u=⟨7,-2,3⟩$ of the point $U,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =u+s\overset{\to }{UV}+t\overset{\to }{UW} \\ r & =⟨7,-2,3⟩+s⟨-3,6,-7⟩+t⟨-4,9,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
